items.title: Security: Community skills distributed under anthropic/ namespace enable trust boundary abuse

items.author: WGlynn
items.body:
Following up on my earlier question about whether external skill contributions are welcome (#1328) with a second concrete one, since these are independently useful.

This skill is compact-memory. A long-running agent spends a lot of context on its own notes and persistent memory, written in prose. Prose is redundant and it drifts: the agent paraphrases an earlier note or quietly softens a rule when it reads it back. The skill has the agent write its internal state in a small fixed symbolic notation instead, one fact per line with a consistent operator set. The result is smaller and reads back

items.title: mcp-builder: evaluation.py scores 0/N against any real MCP server (TextContent not JSON serializable, swallowed into fabricated tool errors)
